facts.title: The National Poet
facts.text: Born in Dsegh, Hovhannes Toumanian became the Poet of All Armenians.

facts.title: Vernatun
facts.text: In his attic, he gathered Armenia's literary elite, including Avetik Isahakyan and Levon Shant.
His poem Anush inspired composer Armen Tigranian's operatic masterpiece.

facts.title: Fables and Epics
facts.text: He adapted the epic David of Sasun and authored the satire A Drop of Honey.

facts.title: At His People's Side
facts.text: He joined relief efforts for refugees, demanding shelter as the Poet of All Armenians.

facts.title: 54 Years Old
facts.text: Afflicted by a serious illness, the writer passed away in Moscow on March 23, 1923.

facts.title: A Living Legacy
facts.text: Two museums are dedicated to him in Armenia, and his name graces a town in Lori.

ytTitle: Hovhannes Toumanian, the Poet of All Armenians
ytLead: Known as the "Poet of All Armenians," Hovhannes Toumanian shaped national culture through his ballads, fables, and epics. A committed writer, he devoted his life to reconciling peoples and helping refugees.
